correctness.rationale: Trilinearity and finite nonnegative layer-cake expansions reduce the theorem to all triples of upsets. The standalone exact integer code checks all 20 upper sets, 1,540 triples, 512 point-triples per case and 64 coefficients per case, with 98,560 nonnegative Bernstein-type coefficients. The polarization identity is derived termwise using three independent replicas and independently checked against direct rational event probabilities for every event triple. Coefficient positivity implies the continuum product-parameter inequality, including boundary points; no inference from sampled parameters occurs.

originality.rationale: The complete biased three-coordinate, arbitrary increasing-function Sahi E3 inequality is a first open dimension beyond the published two-dimensional arbitrary-function theorem. Full primary sources were compared by actual hypotheses and conclusions: neither Kahn's independence rigidity, Lieb--Sahi's two-dimensional theorem, Sahi's restricted-function result, nor Gladkov's equal-intersections theorem implies this general non-sunflower three-bit instance. Semantic published-result searches found no direct equivalent; the limited-coverage and unindexed-priority risks remain and do not constitute a claim of certified worldwide uniqueness.
residual_risks: An unindexed or differently phrased earlier algebraic exhaustive proof of the same three-cube case cannot be ruled out by semantic searches.

Richards (2004) stated an analogous broad inequality with a proof later described by Kahn as incorrect; this does not supply a verified covering theorem, but surviving alternative arguments merit priority review.

value.rationale: This settles the first full three-coordinate Boolean product case beyond the arbitrary-function dimension-two theorem for the published Sahi higher-correlation question. It is a natural complete finite boundary with a globally valid three-parameter positivity certificate and includes truly overlapping non-sunflower events. Its value does not rely on a conjectured downstream theorem, and it is not merely a renamed FKG pair-correlation identity.
